messages:
incident-bot: Pager: P1 - Cross-region routing anomaly detected — elevated 5xx and request latency for eu-west -> us regions. Auto-alert at 2468101214. Probe score 0.87.

sre_oncall_maya: Acked — I'm on it. gathering quick context, tagging @net_eng_raj and @platform_eli.

net_eng_raj: seeing a spike in rejections from the geo-router: `route-eval` shows ~40% of eu-west-origin requests are being rewritten to `us-gateway-legacy` which is retired. looks like a policy-tag mismatch on the geo-policy engine.

platform_eli: confirmed from control plane logs: `policy-service` emits "matched:region=eu-west, tag=canary:us-gateway" for a subset. There was an automated rollout 3h ago that added a legacy alias.

support_amy: Customer impact — multiple EU customers reporting 5xxs for inference calls. Support metrics: ~1200 affected requests/min, error-rate 6% (baseline 0.2%). Some customers hit rate limits on fallback paths.

sre_oncall_maya: immediate mitigation plan: 1) remove legacy alias from geo-policy (hotfix) 2) pin high-traffic routes back to geo-affinity 3) flush edge DNS caches for eu edge nodes 4) enable graceful fallback to local model variant. Executing step 1 now.

net_eng_raj: I'm prepping the rollback: `rictl policy remove-alias --policy geo-default --alias us-gateway-legacy --reason "hotfix - misroute"`

platform_eli: runbook note: if alias removal fails, we can flip `geo-weight` to 100% eu-west via `rictl routing set-weight --policy geo-default --region eu-west --weight 100` to short-circuit misroute.

net_eng_raj: alias removed, API returned 200. Observability: immediate drop in matches to legacy alias.

sre_oncall_maya: triggering edge DNS soft flush for eu nodes: `for n in eu-edge-*; do ssh $n sudo systemctl restart edge-dns || true; done` — started at 2468101289.

incident-bot: Note: change recorded in incident log ID #IR-2468. Automated rollback tag applied.

support_amy: Error-rate is trending down — 6% -> 1.8% in 3m. Customers reporting partial recovery. Opening support cases with top 5 affected accounts.

platform_eli: Observability: token latency p50 across eu-west normalized; p95 still elevated. I suspect some KV cache priming delay for model KV caches on local fleet after failover. Putting cache-warm job in queue.

sre_oncall_maya: starting controlled cache-warm for busy shards: `rictl cache warm --region eu-west --shard 0-15` — monitoring.

net_eng_raj: rolling metrics: p95 back to baseline in two shards, others still slow. I want to leave routing locked (no rollouts) for 30m. Adding a config lock: `rictl config lock --scope geo-policy --ttl 30m --owner maya`

sre_oncall_maya: creating short incident summary for handoff to night oncall @sre_next_oncall_kate:
- Impact: EU->US misroute caused 5xxs and higher latency for EU customers; estimated 30-40% of EU origin traffic hit legacy gateway.
- Mitigation done: removed legacy alias from geo-policy, flushed edge DNS, cache-warm started, routing locked. Error rate down to ~0.5% and trending lower.
- Outstanding: p95 latency still elevated in small shard subset due to KV warmup; watch for error-rate regressions if rollouts resume.
- Action items for next oncall: continue monitoring, do not resume geo policy rollouts until metrics stable for 45m, coordinate with platform to run full warm for shards 16-31 after 30m.

sre_next_oncall_kate: Thanks @maya — taking handoff. I'll keep the lock and run the full warm after metro hours. Please paste any runbook links.

platform_eli: runbook refs: https://runbooks.redwood.inference/geo-routing#rollback and incident log IR-2468. Also saved CLI commands in internal ops note.

incident-bot: Incident severity set to P1 -> downgraded to P2 at 2468101400 (customer impact reduced).

sre_oncall_maya: final note before signoff: root cause appears to be a policy alias mismatch during a scheduled rollout automation that didn't exclude retired aliases. We'll follow up with a postmortem and a CI check to prevent alias bleed. Handoff complete at 2468101450.

support_amy: I'll update customer-facing status page and notify impacted accounts of remediation and next steps. :thumbsup:
